- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or hidden support.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >3%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over 5+ days, model tends to overfit upward trend; apply a mean-reversion correction: cap forecast at 1.5–2% below recent 7-day average.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), sentiment was likely bearish or neutral; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to align with sentiment drift.
